questions.q: What is Intelligence and the Japanese Civilian?
questions.answer: It was a 1945 film produced by the US Marine Corps.

questions.q: What was the purpose of Intelligence and the Japanese Civilian?
questions.answer: To instruct Marines on how they should handle the civilian population of Japan during the post-war occupation.

triples.o: instructing Marines on how they should handle the civilian population of Japan during the post-war occupation

questions.q: What does Intelligence and the Japanese Civilian describe about the Battle of Saipan?
questions.answer: It describes the difficulties the civilian population posed, including the famous mass suicide of Japanese who believed the US would torture them.

triples.o: the difficulties the civilian population posed during the Battle of Saipan including the famous mass suicide of Japanese who believed the US would torture them

questions.q: What role did the Intelligence Division play in the Marianas campaign and at Okinawa?
questions.answer: The Marines learned to use the Intelligence Division to handle the Japanese civilians, and by the time the Marines reached Okinawa, the ID had become a routine part of the operation.

questions.q: Which locations had large Japanese civilian populations at the time of their occupation?
questions.answer: The Marianas and Okinawa, pre-war Japanese possessions, had large Japanese civilian populations at the time of their occupation.

questions.q: What techniques did the Intelligence Division use to handle Japanese civilians?
questions.answer: They made loudspeaker announcements in Japanese to coax them into surrendering; once a group surrendered they found a community leader or someone in a position of authority to make more loudspeaker broadcasts to encourage further surrenders. Camps were set up and made self-sufficient as much as possible.
